title: Koszul tensor towers of K-injective coefficients are inverse-limit acyclic
statement: Let C be a small category with Grothendieck topology J, O a sheaf of commutative rings, r a natural number (including zero), and b a Fin r-indexed family of global sections. Use the actual strict positive Koszul diagram P, its augmentation, dual tensor-tower functor T and ordinary-limit unit of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. Assume derived categories of module sheaves and of strict natural-number inverse towers, and let D be any RingedKoszulLimitPresentation. For every K-injective coefficient complex I, the specified comparison D.comparison at T(I) from the ordinary-limit complex to D.inverseLimit(Q(T(I))) is an isomorphism. No termwise injectivity of I is assumed.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A0A, lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals; Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; more-algebra.tex Tag 0913, lemma-extended-alternating-Cech-is-colimit-koszul; derived.tex Tag 0949, lemma-colim-hocolim

proof.text: Use the finite Koszul dual term computation from lem-weil-pbc-ringed-cech-koszul-dual-kflat. The same two-row total-term induction gives P_m^n=0 for n>r, and the existing nonnegative support gives P_m^n=0 for n<0. Thus its dual is supported in [-r,0]. Dualizing the existing finite-free basis of P_m^(-n), then identifying the finite coproduct and product of unit modules and reindexing by Fin(card S), gives the explicit splitting of each dual term required by lem-weil-pbc-split-perfect-tensor-kinjective. Apply that theorem, and use the componentwise identity chain isomorphism between the transposed strict tower level and the tensor total complex. Hence every tower level is K-injective.

The remaining ordinary-complex calculation is exactly lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-roos-inclusion: the specified zero-second-coordinate comparison from the ordinary limit to the explicit Roos fibre is a quasi-isomorphism. This step does not mention D or a derived-limit presentation.

Resolve the strict tower X by a K-injective tower K with injective terms, using lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence and the tower Grothendieck argument in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit. Evaluation preserves K-injectivity. Products of the levels of both X and K represent derived products by lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective. Naturality of the product comparison conjugates Q(product q) to the product of the levelwise Q(q_n), so it is invertible. The cone triangle and the shift functor imply that the explicit Roos fibre map on q is a quasi-isomorphism, without exactness of arbitrary products. The existing proof of comparison_quasiIso for K only needs its injective terms: its transitions split, and the kernel-to-mapping-fibre comparison of the resulting short exact sequence is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the ordinary-to-Roos comparison now makes Q(lim q) invertible. Finally naturality of D.comparison gives Q(lim q) followed by D.comparison_K equal to D.comparison_X followed by D.inverseLimit(Q q). The first three maps are invertible by the preceding argument, D.comparison_isIso and quasi-isomorphism invariance. Cancel D.inverseLimit(Q q) to conclude.

proof_origin.note: The finite split-perfect level computation and resolution/comparison argument are proved in Lean. Only the strictly ordinary-complex Koszul-to-Roos inclusion remains a named step. No exactness of arbitrary countable products is assumed.
